subject.description: The kind of principal the app serves and verifies (for example "customer"). A lowercase word, since it is also an audit detail key. Any other kind but anonymous acts for subjects.

delegates.description: The kinds of party who act for subjects (sign in through a portal, say), by their word (for example agent), each with its roles. One kind for now.

roles.description: The roles a party of this kind may have, as the policy's role rules name them (for example viewer, clerk). A party with no role, or a role not listed in a rule, is refused what the rule governs.

additionalProperties.description: One kind of party who acts for the app's subjects (for example agent), and the roles one may have.

principals.description: Who the app serves: its subjects, and the parties who act for them with their roles.

name.description: What the level is called, as the policy card says it (for example "verified"). A label: the engine records the number.

factors.description: The slots asked for a step-up to this level (for example accountId, dob), in this order. Each slot id is also the name of the verify tool's param that carries its value.

verify.description: The tool that checks the factors (for example verifyCustomer). Its action in policy.yaml runs only the attempts rule.

failedPrompt.description: The prompt said before the factors are asked again after a failed match. Default "identity_failed".

name.description: What the level is called, as the policy card says it (for example "confirmed by code"). A label: the engine records the number.

length.description: How many digits the code has, 4 to 8. Default 6. The prompts that ask for it say the length in their own words.

otp.description: A one-time code sent to the contact on file and keyed on the keypad: masked, never traced, never a slot.

factors.description: The factors this level adds to level 1: the one-time code, "[{ otp: { length: 6 } }]".

send.description: The tool that sends the one-time code (for example sendCode).

verify.description: The tool that checks the code (for example verifyCode).

2.description: Level 2: level 1 and a one-time code.

levels.description: The identity ladder above level 0 (anonymous), each level with its factors and the tools that check them. Cumulative: level 2 is level 1 and its own factors.

attempts.description: Failed tries allowed at each identity check (the factors, the code) before a person takes the call: what the attempts rule (R6) holds an action to.

signIn.description: What a sign-in proves, for a channel that can sign a caller in (a web portal): the core checks the capability, never the channel's name.

level.description: The level a sign-in proves. It must be the top level of the ladder.

description: identity.yaml: who the app serves and how a caller proves who they are. Leave the file out for an app that verifies no one.
